title: Teen checkup
what: A routine checkup for a teenager: growth, development, vision, posture, and blood pressure. The doctor talks with both the parent and the teen.
why: On the routine checkup schedule, or before school, sports, or college.
duration: usually 30 to 60 minutes with the pediatrician; longer with other doctors
tell_doctor: How your teen sleeps and eats
For girls: if periods have started and how they are

prepare.title: Talk first
prepare.text: Let your teen know the doctor may ask some questions without a parent present. That is normal.

prepare.title: Documents
prepare.text: The medical record and vaccination record.

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: If a fasting blood test is ordered, come in the morning without breakfast.

bring: The medical record and vaccination record
steps: The nurse measures height, weight, and blood pressure
The doctor checks posture, skin, and development
The doctor may ask your teen some questions alone
Sometimes tests or specialists are ordered
The doctor goes over the results with you
feel: Teens may feel awkward. The doctor handles it with care
after: If something is found, more tests will be ordered
The next checkup follows the schedule

faq.q: Why does the doctor talk to my teen without me?
faq.a: Teens are more open about their health that way. The doctor will discuss anything important for safety with you.

faq.q: Is a gynecologist or urologist visit needed?
faq.a: Sometimes they are part of the checkup at certain ages. Ask your clinic.

reminders.text: Teen checkup tomorrow. Bring the medical record, vaccination record, and ID.
